A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, The Lattice Representation Hypothesis of Large Language Models. All 16 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original WordNet experiments on attribute recovery, subsumption inference, and meet/join prediction, with quantitative results and qualitative examples in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original WordNet experiments and results in Section 4, together with the supplementary attribute-correlation analysis in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The half-space framework, normalized projection profiles, soft inclusion and meet/join operators, and attribute-direction and threshold estimation procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five WordNet domains: Animal, Plant, Food, Event, and Cognition. Attribute recovery, partial-order inference, and meet/join task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the Random and Mean comparators alongside Linear for the same models. The meet/join comparison in Figure 4 also retains Random and Mean alongside the proposed operator.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same embedding processing, evaluated models and sizes, precision/recall/F1 and MRR metrics, and sampling of 200 concept pairs per WordNet domain. Dataset counts in Table 4 also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The meet/join case studies, physical-versus-abstract domain comparisons, attribute PCA and correlation analyses, and model-scaling analysis are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the result tables and plots retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–6 retain identical scores, rankings, plotted distributions, correlations, and qualitative examples. No empirical result entries or findings are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, and proofs in Appendices B–C are unchanged. Reflow and equation-spacing adjustments on the early pages do not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same lattice-representation hypothesis, connection between linear representations and FCA, concept-algebra contributions, and empirical claims. The abstract addition concerns resource availability.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of domain differences, attribute correlations, and scaling, together with the proposed neuro-symbolic applications and limitations concerning nonlinear concepts and domain-specific evaluation.

D1.justification: v2's Reproducibility Statement promises code in supplementary materials. v3 retains that paragraph but adds an abstract statement that datasets and code are openly available, with a specific GitHub repository footnote. This adds access guidance; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning in the introduction, Section 5, and Appendix D remain unchanged. The added repository pointer does not introduce another research comparator or related work.

P1.justification: v3 adds one resource-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The longer abstract and new repository footnote reflow text across pages 1–4, with small list/equation-spacing adjustments and renumbering of the ethics footnote. All figures and tables retain their designs and placement.

improvement.justification: The explicit repository pointer provides more actionable code and dataset access guidance than v2's supplementary-material promise, yielding a modest improvement in resource discoverability. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged; the linked resources' completeness and usability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.
